Moonlite Labs|Event marketing & stakeholder engagement|Sep 2026

Bringing an AI creative platform to TIFF's first industry market

I planned and ran Moonlite Labs' seven-day exhibition at TIFF: The Market end to end, from the first approach to the organizers to post-event follow-up, keeping delegates, media, partners, creators and colleagues engaged throughout.

60%+open rates on delegate email campaigns
1 day → severalactivation extended because of strong demand
CBC NewsFounder and CEO interview at the stand
Minister visitCanadian Identity and Culture, at our stand
Read the full case study

Challenge

In September 2026, TIFF launched its first industry market, bringing together the filmmakers, producers and studios Moonlite Labs serves. With a small team and a fixed date, the company had to stand out among 238 exhibitors, show film professionals what the platform could do for their own projects, and turn booth conversations into lasting relationships.

Strategy

I recognized the market's relevance to our target customers, approached the organizers and developed the exhibition and booth activation strategy. I built the plan around participation, inviting delegates to bring their own ideas and watch them become scenes on the spot, and around credibility, with a showcase of work by creators using the platform. Every channel, from email and social media to the booth itself, carried the same message about the creative use of AI.

Execution

  • Delegates. Wrote and sent multiple email campaigns to market delegates, framed around the creative use of AI.
  • Organizers and vendors. Coordinated with the TIFF: The Market team and the vendors managing the booths to keep every requirement and deadline on track.
  • Booth creative and production. Created the booth wall wraps and banners and managed the print vendor from quotes and proofs through printing and delivery.
  • Sizzle reels and partner showcase. Directed our in-house Content Creator to produce sizzle reels for the booth screen, spotlighting work by nine partners and creators, and secured written permission from partners and creators for footage, names, logos and handles, with one consistent credit standard.
  • Script-to-Screen activation. Invited filmmakers and creators to bring about 30 seconds of a script, scene or concept, which live sessions turned into scenes, trailers, proofs of concept and promotional content.
  • Media and government. Coordinated the Founder and CEO's CBC News interview at the stand and facilitated a visit by the Minister of Canadian Identity and Culture.
  • Colleagues and connections. Kept the team informed and engaged before and during market week, and engaged my industry connections and partners around the market.
  • Content. Wrote both TIFF: The Market articles on the company blog, the preview and the highlights recap, and handled social media posting before, during and after the market.
  • At the booth. Spoke with visitors and media, communicated the platform's value propositions to filmmakers, producers and studios, and passed relevant leads to our sales team.
  • Follow-up. Sent post-event follow-up emails to continue the conversations.

Results

  • Every delegate email campaign opened above 60%, reaching up to 2,689 recipients per send.
  • Planned as a one-day event, the Script-to-Screen activation ran for several days because of strong demand from filmmakers and creators.
  • The Founder and CEO's CBC News interview and the Minister's visit gave the company national visibility during the market.
  • Our LinkedIn post of the team at the market drew 1,345 clicks, and conversations at the booth led to follow-up meetings and product demonstrations with prospective clients.

My role

I led the project from start to finish as Moonlite Labs' marketing, communications and partnerships lead, combining strategy with hands-on work in writing, creative, production, media and vendor management.

Moonlite Labs|Social media & content strategy|May – Oct 2026

Building an organic LinkedIn content program from the ground up

As Moonlite Labs' first dedicated marketing hire, I built the company's LinkedIn content program and more than tripled its click-through rate in my first five months, with no paid promotion.

Weighted click-through rate

5% → 17%

Before I joined compared with my first five months
3 → 9posts per month
19%click-through in the latest 90 days
37 → 450reactions
About 4ximpressions per day
Read the full case study

Challenge

When I joined in May 2026, the company page posted about three times a month. Moonlite Labs needed a steady, credible presence to reach filmmakers, studios, brands and partners, and to show what its AI creative platform could do, with organic content only.

Strategy

I set content pillars around product launches, explainers, live event coverage, creator showcases and company news, and made live coverage of the events we attended a central part of the program. I used post-level performance data to decide what to publish more of and shared insights with the Founder and CEO.

Execution

  • Wrote and published every company-page post and managed the content calendar.
  • Briefed and directed our Content Creator on video and visual content, and reviewed and approved each post.
  • Covered Web Summit Vancouver, VivaTech Paris, VRTO and TIFF: The Market live from the floor.
  • Built accessibility into every post with captions, alt text, colour contrast and plain language.
  • Tracked engagement, reach and click-through rate for each post and adjusted the content mix and posting cadence.

Results

  • Weighted click-through rate rose from 5% in the months before I joined to 17% in my first five months, and reached 19% in the latest 90 days.
  • Reactions grew from 37 to 450 and daily impressions roughly quadrupled, as posting rose from three to nine posts a month.
  • Live event coverage became the strongest format, with four event posts drawing more than 2,200 clicks.

My role

I own the channel end to end, from strategy and writing to publishing, community management and performance analysis.

LinkedIn company page analytics, Oct 3, 2025 – Apr 30, 2026 compared with May 1 – Oct 2, 2026. See featured posts.

REC Limited|Public information campaign|Government of India program

Helping millions of households sign up for electricity

For India's national household electrification program, I led a large-scale, multi-channel campaign with state power distribution utilities, turning technical and policy information into human-centred stories in 22 languages.

28.6Mhousehold opt-ins the campaign contributed to
22languages
785,000+Facebook audience for the program
51 pagesimpact book, Lighting Lives
Read the full case study

Challenge

The Government of India set out to connect every willing household to electricity within a tight timeframe, and REC was the program's nodal agency. Many of these households were in remote areas and had never had a connection. People needed to know the program existed, see that it was meant for them and understand how to sign up, in their own language.

Strategy

I built the campaign on human stories backed by program facts. Beneficiary testimonials showed what electricity changed for families, while plain-language information explained the benefits and the steps to join. Working with state power distribution utilities, we carried one consistent message through local languages and channels.

Execution

  • Led a 22-language integrated campaign across multiple channels, coordinating with state power distribution utilities.
  • Translated technical and policy information into accessible messaging for citizens with very different levels of familiarity with the program.
  • Paired beneficiary testimonials with program data to show impact for families and at national scale.
  • Captured the program's story in Lighting Lives, gathering and analyzing program information, shaping the storytelling, overseeing design and production, and managing approvals for accuracy.

Results

  • The campaign contributed to 28.6 million household opt-ins.
  • The program's Facebook audience grew to more than 785,000.
  • Lighting Lives became a lasting record of the program for stakeholders. Read the book

My role

I led communications and coordination for the campaign. Electrification itself was delivered by power distribution utilities and program partners.

REC Limited|Internal communications & employee engagement|Since 2018

Watts Up: an employee magazine by the employees, for the employees

I conceived and launched Watts Up, REC's first multilingual employee publication, and as lead editor built it around the voices of employees at every level and location. The magazine has won awards, earned appreciation from employees and management, and is still published today.

Name

Watts Up

A play on the unit of power and the everyday greeting “What's up?”
Award-winningexternal recognition
Since 2018still in publication
1,000+employees reached in REC and two subsidiaries
25+office locations represented
Read the full case study

Challenge

REC's employees ranged in age from their early twenties to sixty, came from engineering, finance, medicine, the civil service and marketing, and worked in more than 25 locations across India. I saw an opportunity to bring people closer beyond their job titles, help colleagues across generations and functions get to know one another, and give employees in regional offices the same chance to take part as those at the corporate office.

Strategy

I conceived a magazine of the employees, by the employees and for the employees. Contributions were open to everyone, including contract staff, and contributors were published without their designations, so readers met people as colleagues. A mix of sections gave every reader something to enjoy, and a playful tone made the magazine something people chose to pick up.

Execution

  • Editorial direction. As lead editor, set the editorial direction and themes for each issue and built a network of employee contributors in different locations and functions.
  • Sections for every interest. Employee profiles in Up Close & Personal, team introductions in Meet the Team, themed employee articles in Focus, travel writing, stories and poems in Chai Break, company and power-sector news, a history timeline, a library corner, a photo gallery of events and an in-house comic strip.
  • Distribution. Published a web version for all locations, and placed printed copies in a distinctive size at reception, notice boards, waiting areas and libraries to spark curiosity.
  • Recognition for contributors. Thanked every contributor with REC merchandise, and opened a classifieds section for employees and departments to share news and initiatives.

Results

  • Employee contributions grew issue after issue, a key measure of the magazine's popularity.
  • Watts Up won external awards and earned appreciation from both employees and management.
  • The magazine remains in publication years after its first edition in February 2018.
  • It helped create long-term cultural change, giving employees at every level and location a shared space for their work, ideas and lives.

My role

I conceived the publication, launched it and led it as editor, from concept, name and section structure to contributor outreach and each issue's content.
